message.reasoning:
We need to produce a test class for Position.getPositionCost() method. Use JUnit5 (as template uses Jupiter). Need to set up necessary fields: Position objects, CostModels, Trades, maybe mock CostModel to control transaction cost and holding cost.

Goal: test that getPositionCost returns transactionCost + borrowingCost (holding cost). There are two overloads: getPositionCost() (no args) uses transactionCostModel.calculate(this) and getHoldingCost(). So we need to test both scenarios: when position is closed (has entry and exit) and when open (only entry). getHoldingCost() likely returns cost based on holdingCostModel. We can mock CostModel to return known values.

We cannot invoke private methods. Use public constructors.

We need to import classes.

Implementation: Use Mockito to mock CostModel transactionCostModel and holdingCostModel. However Position's transactionCostModel is final transient field set via constructor. We can create Position with custom CostModels via constructor Position(TradeType, CostModel transactionCostModel, CostModel holdingCostModel). That constructor expects startingType, transactionCostModel, holdingCostModel.

We'll also need Trades for entry and exit. Use Trade.buyAt etc. Those static methods likely exist. They require index, price, amount, CostModel maybe. Use transactionCostModel for both trades? Actually Trade.buyAt static method uses transactionCostModel param.

We'll create a transactionCostModel mock that returns a specific Num when calculate(Position) is called. However CostModel.calculate(Position) returns Num. We'll need to stub that.

Similarly holdingCostModel is used in getHoldingCost() which likely calls holdingCostModel.calculate(this). We can mock that as well.

But Position.getHoldingCost() uses holdingCostModel.calculate(this). So we need to stub holdingCostModel.

We'll need a Num implementation: DoubleNum.

We'll create mocks for CostModel transactionModelMock, holdingModelMock.

Set up when(transactionModelMock.calculate(any(Position.class))).thenReturn(DoubleNum.valueOf(5));
when(holdingModelMock.calculate(any(Position.class))).thenReturn(DoubleNum.valueOf(2));

Create a Position with starting type BUY and those models.

Add entry trade: Position.operate(0) will create entry trade using default transaction cost model? Actually operate uses transactionCostModel? In Position implementation, operate creates trades using transactionCostModel? Likely yes. But we can directly set entry via constructor with Trade entry and exit? Simpler: use Position(entry, exit, transactionModelMock, holdingModelMock). Need entry and exit trades with same transaction cost model.

Create entry = Trade.buyAt(0, DoubleNum.valueOf(10), DoubleNum.ONE, transactionModelMock);
exit = Trade.sellAt(5, DoubleNum.valueOf(12), DoubleNum.ONE, transactionModelMock);

Then position = new Position(entry, exit, transactionModelMock, holdingModelMock);

Now call position.getPositionCost() should equal transactionCost + holdingCost = 5+2 = 7.

Also test open position (no exit). Use Position(TradeType.BUY, transactionModelMock, holdingModelMock); then operate entry only. Then getPositionCost should still be transactionCost + holdingCost (holding cost maybe based on open position). We'll stub holding cost accordingly.

Edge: transactionCostModel.calculate(this) may be called each time; we can verify.

Write tests using assertEquals with DoubleNum.

Also test that when transactionCostModel returns NaN? Not needed.

Add @Test methods.

Make sure imports.

Now produce final code.
